chunks: Mālik al-Juhanī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the time of the Dhuhr prayer, and he said:
"When the sun declines, the time of the two prayers has begun. So when you finish your supererogatory prayer, then perform the Dhuhr prayer whenever that appears suitable to you."

key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun declined from its zenith
key_terms.سُبْحَتِكَ: your supererogatory prayer performed before the obligatory prayer
key_terms.وَقْتُ الصَّلَاتَيْنِ: the entered time of the two prayers, Dhuhr and ʿAsr
key_terms.وَقْتِ الظُّهْرِ: the time designated for the Dhuhr prayer

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Dhuhr prayer begin according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that once the sun passes the zenith, the time for both Dhuhr and ʿAsr enters. It also indicates that after completing the recommended nawafil associated with that time, one may perform the Dhuhr prayer thereafter.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.646 - Malik Al-Juhani asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about the time for the Dhuhr (noon) prayer.

Imam (as) replied: "When the sun declines (from its zenith), the time for both (Dhuhr and Asr) prayers begins. So, when you finish your Nawafil (supererogatory prayer), you may perform the Dhuhr prayer whenever you wish."
